newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen lower.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen lower.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open lower Monday, with investors taking their cue from a softer bond market and fearful of a resumption of selling in the high technology sector.
"We had a sloppy day Friday, particularly where the techs were concerned, and I think the opening will reflect that," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.
He said the start of a Robertson Stephens Tech '97 Investors Conference in San Francisco today may spark some strength among high tech issues.
"Sometimes when you have a technology conference of that size, the companies put their best foot forward," he said.

Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said investors should gravitate toward smaller cap high techs and away from the big names that will likely be among the first to go down in the event of a stock market correction.
Cardillo said investors will also likely hang back ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's two-day testimony before Congress starting Wednesday.
